ai.description: The Jeypore Ground Gecko reaches 8 cm in length. It is brownish-grey with dark, irregular dorsal blotches and a distinct, pale, V-shaped mark on the nape. It lacks expanded toe pads.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Jeypore Ground Gecko is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark nuchal collar and a series of dark, wavy transverse bands across its back.
ai.habitat: The Jeypore Ground Gecko inhabits moist deciduous forests and coffee plantations in the Eastern Ghats, typically at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Jeypore Ground Gecko is strictly nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small insects and invertebrates among rocky outcrops and forest floors.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus jeyporensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Jeypore Ground Gecko is endemic to the Eastern Ghats of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, India, typically inhabiting rocky, forested areas at mid-to-high elevations.
